newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't sidesteps vote on reform amendments.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't sidesteps vote on reform amendments.

text.p: Brazil's government claimed a victory in its fight to approve a civil service reform bill Tuesday when it effectively buried four opposition amendments which it claimed were invalid.
The amendments, including one which seeks to maintain jobs-for-life guarantees of public sector workers, will now be ruled on by the Constitution and Justice Committee of the Chamber of Deputies.

The government will only need a straight majority in the committee to rule against the validity of the amendments in the committee, far easier to muster than the three-fifths majorities it needed to defeat them on the floor of the lower house.

Government whips said the move, which was included in a motion approved by the floor of the lower house, was justified because each of the amendments sought to affect more than one article of the bill, contrary to congressional rules.
Opposition deputies were incensed. "This government has just carried out the equivalent of a military coup," said Workers Party deputy Marcelo Deda.
The government also managed to defeat another opposition amendment when 320 members of the lower house voted against a proposal that would have altered rules for the holders of public office.

Voting on other amendments was expected to continue Wednesday and Thursday. Once completed, the bill can be put to a second and final vote on the floor of the lower house. It also has to be approved in the Senate.
